title: Open-extension unit normalization for derived tensor and base change
statement:
Let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be an open immersion of schemes, let
$g:X'\to X$, and form $U'=U\times_X X'$ with $j':U'\hookrightarrow X'$ and
$g_U:U'\to U$ [def-cbc-open-immersion-square]. On the small pro-etale sites
[def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], let $B_X,B_{X'}$ be sheaves of commutative rings
and $g^{-1}B_X\to B_{X'}$ a ring map; put $B_U=j^{-1}B_X$ and
$B_{U'}=j'^{-1}B_{X'}$, with the restricted structural ring map for $g_U$.
Work in the ordinary unbounded derived categories of these module sheaves
[def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category].
Use exact extension by zero $j_!,j'_!$ on the localized ringed sites
[def-pur-localized-ringed-site, lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact],
canonical derived module pullback and tensor
[lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], and the canonical
pullback-composition isomorphism $\theta:j'^*Lg^*\cong Lg_U^*j^*$.

The open adjunction units $u_M:M\to j^*j_!M$ and $u'_{M'}:M'\to j'^*j'_!M'$
are isomorphisms, in the normalization whose section over an object factoring
through the open is that same section. Extension by zero is fully faithful
on these derived categories. There are canonical natural isomorphisms
$$\beta_M:Lg^*j_!M\xrightarrow{\sim}j'_!Lg_U^*M,\qquad
\gamma_{M,N}:j_!M\otimes^L_{B_X}N\xrightarrow{\sim}
j_!(M\otimes^L_{B_U}j^*N).$$
Here $M\in D(B_U)$ and $N\in D(B_X)$ are arbitrary. The inverse of $\beta_M$
is the $j'_!\dashv j'^*$-adjunct of $Lg_U^*u_M$, followed by $\theta^{-1}$;
the inverse of $\gamma_{M,N}$ is the $j_!\dashv j^*$-adjunct of
$u_M\otimes1$ under the canonical restriction/tensor comparison. After the
open unit identifications, $j'^*\beta_M$ and $j^*\gamma_{M,N}$ are the
identity maps under these specified pullback and tensor identifications.
For constant finite $B_X=B_{X'}=A$ these are precisely the canonical maps of
[lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-base-change] and
[lem-cbc-extension-zero-projection-formula]. These assertions also hold for
the ringed diagram topoi of strict coefficient systems, using their
termwise open extensions and derived system pullbacks and tensors
[lem-pur-coefficient-system-derived-comparison].
